chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hanafiyya (al-Halabi), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a free woman whom her husband (who is a slave) accuses (of adultery), he said: They perform li'an (mutual imprecation).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of li'an when a slave husband accuses his free wife of adultery?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that the status of the husband as a slave does not invalidate the li'an procedure when he accuses his free wife, a ruling derived from the principle that the marital bond remains intact despite the status disparity. It highlights the juristic consensus in Shia tradition that the specific procedural requirements of li'an are tied to the existence of marriage rather than the social rank of the spouses. This ensures legal consistency in divorce and paternity denial cases across different social strata.
